scope: Task priority as a persisted task attribute.
Filtering the task collection by priority.

constraints: C01: Existing task CRUD behavior must remain valid unless directly affected by the new priority requirement.
C02: Priority values are closed to exactly LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.
C03: The requirement must be represented in ISR-derived requirements/contracts, not hidden in implementation code.
C04: The evolution engine must remain implementation-technology neutral.
C05: Architecture selection must remain downstream of candidate generation.
C06: No implementation may be selected merely for ease of implementation.
C07: Existing security, validation, and failure-closed behavior must be preserved.
C08: The change must remain attributable to VS1-OBJ-001.
C09: Historical D01-D22 artifacts remain immutable.
C10: The existing ISR remains the constitutional source of truth.
objective.objective_statement: Evolve the VS1 TaskFlow product so that tasks support an explicit priority attribute with the values LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH, and users can view and filter tasks by priority, while preserving all existing TaskFlow behavior and existing CRUD obligations.

in_scope: Task priority as a persisted task attribute.
Allowed priority values LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.
Display of task priority in the existing task UI.
Filtering the task collection by priority.
API/backend contracts required to support the capability.
Database/schema changes required by the capability.
Generated and existing tests required to verify the capability.
Documentation/contracts directly affected by the requirement.
out_of_scope: Replacement of the existing framework or language stack.
Migration to a different database technology.
Performance optimization unrelated to priority filtering.
Changes to the evolutionary engine itself.
Changes to the canonical ISR unless separately authorized.

security_constraints: SEC01: Existing authentication and authorization behavior must not be weakened.
SEC02: Priority must not become an authorization mechanism.
SEC03: Unauthorized users must not gain task data access through filtering.
SEC04: Input validation must reject malformed or unsupported priority values.
SEC05: Existing secret-handling and credential boundaries remain unchanged.
SEC06: Existing audit/evidence requirements remain preserved.

success_criteria.criterion: SC01: Every task has a valid priority after migration/defaulting.
success_criteria.measurement: every persisted task carries LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH after migration.

success_criteria.criterion: SC02: API creates tasks with LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH priority.
success_criteria.measurement: POST create returns 201 for each of LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.

success_criteria.criterion: SC03: API updates existing task priority.
success_criteria.measurement: PATCH update changes priority, 200 with new value.

success_criteria.criterion: SC04: API returns priority on retrieval.
success_criteria.measurement: GET single/list responses include priority field.

success_criteria.criterion: SC05: Invalid priority values rejected deterministically.

success_criteria.measurement: rendered task view shows priority label.

success_criteria.criterion: SC07: Users filter task collection by priority.
success_criteria.measurement: filtered listing returns exactly matching tasks.

success_criteria.criterion: SC08: Existing CRUD acceptance tests pass.
SC10: Selected candidate satisfies priority requirement without violating obligations.
success_criteria.measurement: selected candidate evidence cites SC01-SC09 PASS.

success_criteria.criterion: SC11: Deployment succeeds via existing VS1 deployment path.
success_criteria.measurement: deployment health + smoke PASS via VS1 path.

success_criteria.criterion: SC12: Runtime observation demonstrates the priority capability.
success_criteria.measurement: observation records show priority operations PASS.

success_criteria.criterion: SC13: Evidence chain traceable objective to decision.
success_criteria.measurement: each link resolves: objective to decision record.
